sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *a pesar de que* and *pese a* from B1 Unit 32, and *aunque* from A2 Unit 28. They let you say that something happened or lasted in spite of a difficulty, which is the story of Antigua: thick walls, earthquakes and families who stayed. With a real fact, the verb is in the indicative.

sections.title: Forms with a pesar de and pese a
rows: A pesar de los terremotos, la ciudad siguió viva.
*a pesar de* + noun: in spite of the earthquakes, the city lived on
A pesar de ser muy sólida, la iglesia sufrió daños.
*a pesar de* + infinitive: although it was very solid, the church was damaged
A pesar de que los muros eran gruesos, hubo daños.
*a pesar de que* + a full clause: although the walls were thick, there was damage
Pese a las órdenes, muchas familias se quedaron.
*pese a* + noun: despite the orders, many families stayed

items.spanish: Pese a los terremotos, los constructores siguieron usando piedra.
items.english: Despite the earthquakes, the builders kept using stone.

items.spanish: A pesar de que la capital se trasladó, muchas familias se quedaron.
items.english: Although the capital was moved, many families stayed.

items.spanish: A pesar de ser una ciudad antigua, hoy recibe a muchos visitantes.
items.english: Although it is an old city, today it receives many visitors.

items.spanish: Pese a su fachada sencilla, la iglesia es muy sólida.
items.english: Despite its plain facade, the church is very solid.

sections.content: Before a full clause you need *que*: *a pesar de que los muros eran gruesos*. Before a noun or an infinitive you do not: *a pesar de los muros*, *a pesar de ser gruesos*. Not *a pesar que*, and not *a pesar de los muros eran gruesos*.
